context: A small private language school in Shinjuku. Hiroshi (retired professor) has been asked by Asuka to give a one-off Saturday talk to advanced students. He has come early; she's showing him around.
purpose: peer-to-peer professional warmth — two teachers recognising each other

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 先生、本日はわざわざ、ありがとうございます。
lines.en: Sensei — thank you so much for coming today.
lines.style: Formal, steady respect. The breath of someone greeting a guest they genuinely admire. Slight bow of the head audible in the voice. No performance — just sincere.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いえ、こちらこそ。お招きいただいて。
lines.en: No, no — thank you for inviting me.
lines.style: Mirrors her formality with quiet grace. Each word given its own small space. A gentle bow folded into the phrasing, not rushed.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.style: Genuine observation, not small talk. A beat of warmth underneath. The kind of thing said when you actually mean it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん、なんとか。学生たちは、何人くらい？
lines.en: Managing, more or less. How many students are coming today?
lines.style: Practical pivot. The 「なんとか」 lands with one quiet beat — honest about age without complaint. Steady, forward-moving.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 今日は十二名です。少なめで、すみません。
lines.en: Twelve today. Smaller than I'd have liked — I'm sorry.
lines.style: Apologetic undertone, though she's already worried. Slight tension in the shoulders. Quick words, as if moving past the moment before he can reassure her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いえいえ。少ないほうが、いい話になる。
lines.en: No, no. A smaller group makes for better conversation.
lines.style: The certainty of experience. Warm and settling. The kind of line that lands like a hand on a shoulder — immediately reassuring.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 先生、そうおっしゃると思いました。
lines.en: I had a feeling you'd say that, sensei.
lines.style: A small smile breaking through. Fondness audible. The kind of moment when a junior teacher realizes the elder one sees exactly what she needed to hear.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: (small chuckle)私も、教師、長くやっただけある。
lines.en: (small chuckle) Well, I've been teaching a long time.
lines.style: A real, warm chuckle — the sound of someone who enjoys the joke of his own experience. Shared understanding between two people who've lived the same work.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: お時間、ぴったり一時間で大丈夫ですか？
lines.en: Is exactly one hour alright for you?
lines.style: Practical check-in. Warm but efficient. The tone of someone managing details with genuine care, not anxiety.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん、ちょうど。…一緒に、お茶でも？前に。
lines.en: Yes, perfect. …Shall we have tea together first?
lines.style: A small unexpected gentleness opens the door. Not rushed. The suggestion sits like an invitation, not a question. Quiet pleasure in his own idea.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.en: Of course. I'll have it ready right away.
lines.style: Genuine warmth breaks through. A real smile in the voice. Already turning — moving toward the kitchen with purpose and grace.
